findings.title: Second `self.downsize` overrides the first and breaks the emoji resize job
findings.body: `downsize` is defined twice (lines 145 and 149). Ruby keeps the last one, so the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` version is dead code. The new signature is `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, which takes at most 4 arguments. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14). That raises `ArgumentError`, so custom emoji are never downsized to 100x100. Remove one definition and make the callers agree. Either update resize_emoji.rb to pass `"100x100"`, or keep the width/height form and have the controller pass `"80%"` another way.

findings.title: Downsize loop on the upload tempfile: GIF animation check and stale size
findings.body:
1) `optimize` only picks the animated (gifsicle) path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Rack upload tempfile paths and `FileHelper.download` temp paths may not end in `.gif`, so `allow_animation` has no effect. The ImageMagick `downsize_instructions` uses `from[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF would be flattened to its first frame. That is silent data loss. Pass an extension-bearing path or check the filename.
2) The return value of `downsize` is ignored. If `convert` fails, the loop runs 5 times and then falls through. `tempfile.size` on a Tempfile may also be cached/buffered, so the loop condition may not see the rewritten file. Check the result and use `File.size(tempfile.path)`.
If the image is still too big after 5 attempts, `Upload.create_for` rejects it with a size error, which is acceptable.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores the max_attachment_size_kb setting
findings.body: The client check now uses a fixed 10MB for every type. Server-side validation still applies `max_#{type}_size_kb` (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81). The server auto-downsizes images only, not attachments. So an attachment between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB now passes the client check and is uploaded in full, then rejected asynchronously. A site with `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload attachments of that size at all. Keep the setting for non-image types (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_attachment_size_kb']`) and use the 10MB cap only for images.

findings.title: 413 message hardcodes 10 MB while the web server limit is the max_*_size_kb setting
findings.body: The setting descriptions say it must match nginx `client_max_body_size`. A 413 from the web server therefore reports the limit configured in nginx, not a fixed 10MB. The message now shows a number that may be wrong. The same hardcoded value is duplicated at line 182 and in uploads_controller.rb:55. Consider a single shared constant.

contracts.action: Oversized image upload is downsized server-side before Upload.create_for
contracts.equivalent_path: OptimizedImage.resize in app/models/upload.rb:98 (in-place resize of a tempfile)
contracts.before_after: Before: images over max_image_size_kb were rejected by Upload.create_for validation. After: they are shrunk by 80% up to 5 times, then validated.
contracts.visible_effect: User sees the upload succeed with a smaller image, or a size error via MessageBus if still too large.
contracts.failure_mode: The return value of downsize is ignored. A failing convert is silent and the validator then rejects the file. GIF animation may be lost because the tempfile path may lack a .gif extension.

contracts.before_after: Before: 5-arg call worked. After: the last definition accepts at most 4 args, so the call raises ArgumentError.

summary: Blocker: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice, and the second definition accepts at most 4 arguments. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` still calls it with 5, so it raises `ArgumentError` and emoji are no longer resized. I also flagged two other problems. The upload downsize loop can drop GIF animation and ignores failures. The hardcoded 10MB client limit bypasses `max_attachment_size_kb`. I read the three files in full plus `resize_emoji.rb`. I did not read `upload.rb` or `upload_validator.rb` in full, only the grep hits.
